newsitem.title: USA: British man arraigned on NJ fraud charges.
newsitem.headline: British man arraigned on NJ fraud charges.

text.p: A British man who was extradited to the United States from Switzerland pleaded not guilty Thursday to charges that he conspired with others to defraud investors of $4.32 million.
David Dunn, 53, was allegedly involved in a bogus trust named the Euro-American Money Fund Trust. A New Jersey man controlled its interests in the United States.

At his arraignment before Judge Garrett E. Brown in U.S. District Court in Trenton, Dunn pleaded not guilty to charges of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud. He was indicted by a grand jury in January last year and Dunn has been detained in a Swiss prison since March.
He was ordered held without bail and a hearing was scheduled for March 4.
Dunn, whose hometown was given as Wallingford in England, has had a home in Geneva, Switzerland for many years, officials said.
He was extradited to the United States Jan. 9 after his appeal of the extradition order was denied by the Swiss Supreme Court.

The victims of the alleged fraud were Ingo-Pet, a German company that was acting in partnership with a Russian company called Ljukon. They were induced to pay a $4.32 million advance fee in order to buy what Dunn and his co-conspirators called a "Master Collateral Commitment", the statement said.

According to Dunn's indictment, John Voigt, formerly of Linwood, New Jersey, was a director of Euro-American who controlled operations in the United States. Voigt was convicted in 1994 with two other people in New Jersey and is serving a 15-year sentence in a federal jail.
